questions.title: Scalar control-variate variance reduction with a fixed coefficient
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation in Monte Carlo variance reduction. Let (X_i,C_i), i=1,...,n, be iid paired real observations with E[C_i]=0, finite second moments, Var(X_i)>0, and Var(C_i)>0. The target is alpha=E[X_i]. For a fixed finite scalar lambda supplied independently of the current sample, study alpha_hat_lambda=bar(X)-lambda*bar(C). Develop one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX derivation of exact unbiasedness, the exact finite-sample variance quadratic, the variance-minimizing population coefficient lambda*=Cov(X,C)/Var(C), the minimized variance and its correlation form, and the fixed-lambda central limit theorem with consistent studentization. State the moment, nondegeneracy, fixed-coefficient, and iid-pairing conditions; distinguish population optimality from estimating lambda on the same data and distinguish simulation support from proof. The required model-authored artifact is est_scalar_control_variate and must implement the frozen run_estimator(request) contract exactly. Exploratory computation may diagnose algebra or implementation. A separate frozen confirmatory assessment uses independently generated paired samples under predeclared Gaussian and non-Gaussian finite-moment laws, supplies the population-optimal fixed coefficient, checks exact moment and transformation identities, and assesses variance reduction plus approximate centered unit-normal studentized behavior with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Source-code replication and novelty are not applicable. Lean formalization is not applicable to this focused nonformal capability task.

request_fields.name: x
request_fields.meaning: The finite real-valued target-output sample, paired by position with control.
request_fields.shape: length n with n>=4, equal to len(control), and strictly positive Bessel-corrected sample variance
request_fields.indexing: zero-based entries x[j] and control[j] form observation pair j
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries, fewer than four observations, unequal sample lengths, and a nonpositive sample variance of x.

request_fields.name: control
request_fields.meaning: The finite real-valued control sample whose population mean is known by the task setup to equal zero, paired by position with x.
request_fields.shape: length n with n>=4 and equal to len(x)
request_fields.indexing: zero-based entries x[j] and control[j] form observation pair j
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries, fewer than four observations, and unequal sample lengths. The sample mean need not be zero.

request_fields.name: control_coefficient
request_fields.meaning: The fixed finite scalar lambda in bar(x)-lambda*bar(control), supplied independently of the current sample.
request_fields.indexing: one coefficient applied to every paired observation
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric values, and nonfinite values.

response_fields.name: n_observations
response_fields.meaning: The number n of paired observations used by every returned quantity.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be an integer at least four.
response_fields.normalization: No normalization; count each pair exactly once.

response_fields.name: mean_x
response_fields.meaning: The arithmetic mean of the supplied target-output sample.
response_fields.indexing: uses all n entries of x

response_fields.name: mean_control
response_fields.meaning: The arithmetic mean of the supplied control sample.
response_fields.indexing: uses all n entries of control
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be JSON-finite and need not equal the known population mean zero.

response_fields.name: control_coefficient
response_fields.meaning: The exact fixed coefficient supplied in the request.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be JSON-finite and exactly preserve the request value.

response_fields.name: direct_estimate
response_fields.meaning: The conventional Monte Carlo estimate of alpha.

response_fields.name: adjusted_estimate
response_fields.meaning: The fixed-coefficient control-variate estimate of alpha.

response_fields.name: sample_variance_x
response_fields.meaning: The ordinary Bessel-corrected sample variance of x.
response_fields.indexing: uses all n centered target outputs
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be JSON-finite and strictly positive.

response_fields.name: sample_variance_control
response_fields.meaning: The ordinary Bessel-corrected sample variance of control.
response_fields.indexing: uses all n centered control values

response_fields.name: sample_covariance_x_control
response_fields.meaning: The ordinary Bessel-corrected paired sample covariance of x and control.
response_fields.indexing: preserves the supplied pairing and uses all n pairs

response_fields.name: adjusted_sample_variance
response_fields.meaning: The Bessel-corrected sample variance of x[j]-control_coefficient*control[j].
response_fields.indexing: uses every adjusted paired observation exactly once

response_fields.name: direct_standard_error
response_fields.meaning: The usual estimated standard error of the direct sample mean.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be JSON-finite and strictly positive.

response_fields.name: adjusted_standard_error
response_fields.meaning: The usual estimated standard error of the fixed-coefficient adjusted sample mean.

response_fields.name: estimated_variance_ratio
response_fields.meaning: The estimated per-observation variance of the adjusted output divided by that of the direct output.
response_fields.indexing: uses the two returned sample variances
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be JSON-finite and nonnegative because sample_variance_x is required to be positive.

invariants.meaning: All returned moments use the declared n-1 normalization; direct_estimate equals mean_x; adjusted_estimate equals mean_x-control_coefficient*mean_control; adjusted_sample_variance equals sample_variance_x-2*control_coefficient*sample_covariance_x_control+control_coefficient^2*sample_variance_control; both standard errors square to their corresponding sample variance divided by n; and estimated_variance_ratio equals adjusted_sample_variance/sample_variance_x.

With control_coefficient=0, adjusted_estimate, adjusted_sample_variance, adjusted_standard_error, and estimated_variance_ratio exactly recover direct_estimate, sample_variance_x, direct_standard_error, and one.

Multiplying every control value by a nonzero finite a and dividing control_coefficient by a preserves adjusted_estimate, adjusted_sample_variance, adjusted_standard_error, and estimated_variance_ratio while mean_control, sample_variance_control, and sample_covariance_x_control scale according to their units.

Adding a finite constant d to every x value increases mean_x, direct_estimate, and adjusted_estimate by d while preserving all returned variances, covariance, standard errors, and estimated_variance_ratio.

empirical_claims.meaning: The frozen confirmatory assessment supplies each predeclared law's population-optimal fixed coefficient, compares direct and adjusted sampling variance, and assesses (adjusted_estimate-alpha)/adjusted_standard_error for approximate centered unit-normal behavior with Monte Carlo uncertainty; this is empirical support rather than proof.

Every confirmatory estimator call uses the exact predeclared paired sample and fixed coefficient, and the assessment separately verifies returned moments, covariance, the adjusted variance quadratic, standard errors, variance ratio, zero-coefficient recovery, rescaling, and shift identities before aggregating sampling behavior.
